title: Manganese Sulphate Q3 2026 Price Review
gist: Chinese manganese sulphate (32% EXW) was range-bound in Q3 2026, ending at RMB 7,116/t (+1.1% q/q), as firm sulphur/acid, ore and freight costs offset muted battery demand. LMFP is not yet supporting demand, so Benchmark expects cost pass-through, not chemistry shifts, to drive the next move.

insights.claim: Benchmark's Manganese Sulphate (32%) EXW China price ended Q3 2026 at RMB 7,116/tonne ($1,060/tonne), up only 1.1% from end-Q2, after trading in a tight band between RMB 7,043 (mid-July low) and RMB 7,178 (high later in July).
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Price is range-bound; low realized volatility offers little directional edge in the quarter.

insights.claim: The quiet Q3 followed a Q1 surge driven by high sulphuric acid prices and cancellation of export tax rebates on NCM precursors and cathode materials, and a small Q2 correction as off-season downstream operating rates slowed and idled capacity restarted.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Policy (rebate cancellation) and input costs, not demand, drove the year's big move.

insights.claim: Seasonal restocking, tight supply and firm feedstock costs held manganese sulphate steady, and Benchmark's head of prices expects the next move to come from cost pass-through rather than a shift in cathode chemistry demand.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Watch input costs rather than cathode demand as the leading indicator for price direction.
insights.quote: the next move is more likely to come from cost pass-through than from any shift in cathode chemistry demand

insights.claim: Battery-grade demand is a small fraction of total manganese consumption, which insulated manganese sulphate from the sharper price moves seen in lithium, nickel and rare earths.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Manganese sulphate is a low-beta battery-materials exposure compared with lithium or nickel.
insights.locator: Why has manganese sulphate stayed within such a tight range?

insights.claim: Manganese sulphate did not follow the sharper sulphur spikes that hit Indonesian HPAL nickel earlier in the year, likely because China's domestic acid production relies less on Middle Eastern sulphur imports, so costs acted as a floor rather than a driver of gains.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Sulphur shocks transmit unevenly; Chinese manganese is a cost-floor story, limiting upside from Middle East disruptions unless they widen.

insights.claim: Lack of sulphuric acid availability has reduced spot-market activity in manganese, with some producers holding inventory below recommended safe thresholds, so tight sulphate supply is unlikely to ease in the short term.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Supply tightness supports prices even with weak battery demand.
insights.locator: Why has manganese sulphate stayed within such a tight range?

insights.claim: High-purity manganese sulphate monohydrate (HPMSM) production is effectively 100% exposed to sulphur and sulphuric acid market shocks, a higher share than lithium, cobalt or rare earths.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: HPMSM is the most sulphur-sensitive battery material; use sulphur/acid prices as a leading indicator.
insights.locator: How exposed is manganese sulphate to the sulphur cost pressures

insights.claim: Sulphuric acid prices rose 25% year-on-year in Q2 on high sulphur prices, which together with firm ore quotations and soaring freight rates leaves producers little room for price concessions.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Cost floor under prices; margin compression risk for producers who cannot pass costs on.

insights.claim: Only two Chinese cathode producers are understood to be shipping LMFP, in small volumes, and a major Chinese battery maker has repeatedly confirmed its second-generation flagship LFP battery contains no manganese.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: LMFP adoption is not yet a credible manganese demand catalyst.
insights.locator: Is LMFP providing any real support to battery-grade demand?

insights.claim: Manganese dissolution weakens cycling performance, so few manufacturers prioritise LMFP in R&D and prefer investing in fifth-generation LFP; Q3 price support came from supply and cost conditions, not a shift to manganese-bearing cathodes.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Technical barrier caps chemistry-driven manganese upside until dissolution is solved.
insights.locator: Is LMFP providing any real support to battery-grade demand?

insights.claim: Tropical Cyclone Narelle cut a major Australian producer's Q3 ore output to 589,000wmt and lowered full-year guidance, but diversified ore sourcing has so far kept the disruption out of Chinese sulphate pricing.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Ore shortfall is a latent upside risk to Chinese feedstock costs if rebound disappoints.

insights.claim: Renewed Middle East-related sulphur disruption or higher freight rates could test producers' ability to pass costs to buyers in Q4, and the pace of Australian ore recovery after Cyclone Narelle is a key variable.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Q4 catalysts for a breakout from the range are cost-side, not demand-side.
insights.locator: What should manganese market participants watch in Q4?

insights.claim: Western nations aim to diversify HPMSM supply away from China's dominant share, and Benchmark will watch European and North American HPMSM projects; a change in battery chemistry mix would matter only if LMFP overcomes dissolution or high-manganese NMC gains traction.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Ex-China HPMSM projects are a longer-dated supply-diversification theme to monitor.
insights.locator: What should manganese market participants watch in Q4?
